entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent and is externally grounded in a normative or legal system. It is not internally grounded (so not a Disposition), and it is not a measurable scalar property (so not a Quality). Rather, it is a social-normative role: the agent bears a binding qua occupant of a position defined by the obligation structure. This maps naturally to BFO Role (BFO_0000023). The existing working class LegalObligation is already typed as a Role (BFO_0000023), but AgentObligationBinding is more specific: it captures the relational binding of a particular agent to an obligation, i.e., the role the agent plays as the one bound by the obligation. A subclass of BFO_0000023 is warranted rather than reusing LegalObligation directly because LegalObligation represents the obligation itself as a role-type, whereas AgentObligationBinding represents the agent-side relational pole of that normative tie.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a kind of Role: it is a specifically dependent continuant externally grounded in a normative structure, inhering in the agent who is bound.
Role is a subclass of Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020); making this explicit supports reasoner inference that instances of AgentObligationBinding inhere in a bearer (the agent).

open_questions: Should AgentObligationBinding be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation (itself typed as BFO_0000023), or kept as a direct subclass of BFO_0000023? The distinction depends on whether LegalObligation is intended to represent the obligation as borne by the obligee (agent-side) or as a normative object in the legal system.

Is the 'agent' in 'agent-obligation binding' always a legal person/institution, or also a moral agent? This affects whether bearer constraints should reference working:LegalInstitution or a broader Agent class.

Should 'agent-obligation binding' be further distinguished from 'agent-right binding' as a dual correlative (Hohfeld-style), and if so, should a common parent class (e.g., NormativePositionBinding) be introduced?
Is this intended as a class (a kind of binding) or as a specific individual instance of a particular obligation binding a particular agent?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the normative tie whereby a specific agent is bound by an obligation. In BFO terms, this is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent as its bearer, and its existence is externally grounded in a normative/legal system rather than in the agent's intrinsic nature (which would instead indicate a Disposition). The class is distinct from the existing working:LegalObligation, which represents the obligation-type as a role in the system, whereas AgentObligationBinding foregrounds the agent-side pole of the binding relation. A new class working:AgentObligationBinding is proposed as a direct subclass of BFO_0000023, with an explicit subClassOf BFO_0000020 to support SDC reasoning. Key open questions concern the relationship to LegalObligation, the scope of 'agent,' and whether a Hohfeldian correlative structure is intended.
